**Beta** from `{{REF}}` @ {{SHA}}: the next version, being tested before it becomes a stable release, so it can still change. For the stable version, take the latest release (not a beta). A server and its players need the same beta.

**New since 3.6.0 (beta): style, blood and a minimap.** A HELLISH rank above SSS and a restyled STYLE panel; from S up each rank gives a little more speed, attack speed and reach while you hold it. A hell weapon whose Blood Art is ready burns with a blood aura on its hotbar slot instead of the glint. A thin Blood Oath meter rests on the stamina bar. A minimap in a corner (Y for settings, Z and X to zoom, B to mark where you stand) with a cave view, dots for players, monsters and animals, Rests, waymarks and the way down. The HUD's pieces now keep out of each other's way, boss bars and effects too.

**New since 3.5.0 (beta): fewer, clearer messages.** Every message Hellcraft shows now appears in one small box above the hotbar, in one style: what characters say, Virgil's tips, notices, headlines (circle cards, Paradiso's spheres, trials, prestige, a guardian's name, which no longer fill the middle of the screen) and quick status words like "Parried!" in a slim line under it. Messages queue with the important ones first, repeats are dropped, a "+n" shows how many wait, and each stays long enough to read. Virgil talks less: no tips mid-fight or during cutscenes, at least 30 seconds between tips, shorter lessons, and none that describe what you can already see or repeat a circle's card. Entering a circle shows just its card now.

**New since 3.5.0 (beta): Hellcraft sounds like itself.** Every sound the mod makes is its own now instead of a borrowed vanilla one: the guardians and Lucifer's two bodies roar, swing and slam with their own voices; every monster of Hell has its own cries; blocks, guards, parries, rolls and swings ring like steel; the Blood Altars, hearts, candles, relics, travel and the hell weapons' Blood Arts all have their own sounds; and each circle has its own ambience (wind, rain, bubbling swamp, burning tombs, cracking ice, the wingbeat far off), the Forge of Dis its furnaces. **Music:** each region has its own track (the Dark Wood, the Vestibule, Limbo, Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Dis, Heresy, the circles of Violence, Malebolge, Cocytus, the Forge of Dis, Purgatory, Paradiso and the Empyrean), and Lucifer's fight has three, one per phase, in place of the vanilla discs. **Boss music:** every guardian (Minos, Cerberus, Plutus, Phlegyas, the Furies, Farinata, the Minotaur, Geryon, Vulcan and the Seraph) has its own fight music, and when it rages at half health the music changes to its second, fiercer track. Subtitles name every sound. Turn the music down with the Music slider and the ambience with Ambient/Environment, as usual. No new world needed.

**New in 3.5 (beta): hit what you see.** Cerberus's three heads and necks, Geryon's head, coils and sting, and Minos's tail can be struck now, wherever the model puts them as they move (before, only a box round the middle of each boss counted, so a blow at Cerberus's snapping heads hit nothing). Blows and arrows there hurt the boss as anywhere else.

**New in 3.5 (beta): mob health bars.** A hurt mob (or the one you're looking at) shows its health in a bar over its head: red for monsters, green for animals, and a pale stretch shows what your last blow took before it drains away. Bosses keep their boss bar. Want it beside the mob instead? `/hellcraft-client healthbars side` (or `off`, or `above` to put it back; only for you).

**New in 3.5 (beta): guard any time.** Raising your guard no longer waits for a swing or a roll to finish: it cuts a swing short (a blow stopped in its wind-up never lands, so you can also feint), and it cuts a roll short as soon as you're back up off the ground and blows no longer slip past you. Hold it a little early and it goes up the moment it can. **Heavy weapons commit:** with an axe, a mace, the Reaper or the Tithe Axe, once your blow lands you're committed until the swing ends (a guard held then goes up as it ends), but you're braced and take a quarter less damage until then. **Fixed:** with Sidestep leggings, a guard raised late in a roll could show on your screen while blocking nothing; and a swing straight after guarding out of one no longer whiffs without landing. **First person and the roll:** every swing reads in first person now: raised before the blow, sweeping through the middle of the view and finishing where you can see it, never dropping behind the hotbar (the heavy blows chop down through the middle; the thrust drives straight ahead; a broken guard knocks the blade aside instead of out of sight). Your weapon moves with you in first person: it sways with your stride, swings side to side when sprinting, lifts as you jump and drops when you land (with View Bobbing on). A bow, a shield or food eases into place and back instead of snapping, and loosing an arrow, firing a crossbow or taking a blow on a shield kicks. **Rolling makes you small:** under a block high for most of the roll, so there's less of you to hit and you can roll under a one-block gap (come up in one and you crawl out). **Every player moves smoothly.** Walking, sprinting (leaning in, arms pumping), sneaking, standing (a slow breath), jumping, long falls and landings (the knees give, and a hard landing dips your view) are all animated, timed to your real footsteps, and running round a bend leans into it. Bows are drawn back as they charge and the string hand flies back when you loose; shields are braced behind and rock when struck; food and drink go to the mouth; crossbows kick and tridents are whipped over in a throw. Crouching and raising a bow or shield ease in instead of snapping. Don't like it? `/hellcraft-client animations off` (only for you; `on` turns it back on). **New in 3.5 (beta), after the first combat playtest:** **Blood Art key:** a full hell weapon's Blood Art now has its own key, **R** (Controls, Hellcraft); the "fully charged" message names it (it still said right-click, which now raises the guard). **Lovers' dives can be blocked from above:** a blow from close overhead counts as faced, and a dive is judged by where it came from. **Style rewards skill, not weapon swapping:** each move of your weapon's chain goes stale on its own, so playing the chain through stays fresh and mashing one cut doesn't; feats (a finisher, a heavy blow, a timed parry, a riposte, a dodge through a blow, a counter, a Blood Art) raise a **multiplier** up to **x2**, shown on the style panel, and getting hit resets it. A guard just held up scores a little; a timed parry scores a lot. Lucifer's fight counts your dodges too. **Fights can be read by ear:** Hellcraft's first sounds of its own. Every boss's danger marks now sound as they come: **red**, a low horn that swells and thumps as the blow lands; **white**, a bright shimmer rising to a hard ring on the very moment to have your guard up; **purple**, a sour rising whine (jump or roll). Parries ring, broken guards clang, and a blow slipping through your roll whooshes. **The Fallen Seraph fights like a swordsman now:** short strings of blows picked by how far away you are, each with its own look and sound, at full speed: a **flurry** of three cuts on three chimes (parry all three and he breaks), a **feint** whose blade hangs humming and falls late on a ring (a guard raised at the usual time is too early), a **dive** onto a circle that follows you to the last moment (roll out late and he's stuck in the ice), a **crescent** of light along the ice (jump or roll), and once he snaps a **counter stance** (wings folded, humming: don't strike, wait and he's open) and a **blink** behind you (turn and parry on the ring). The stars come only now and then. His wing guard is gone: instead a **posture bar** under his health wears down with every blow, parry and dodged blow, and when it breaks he kneels and takes half as much again (blows on him then score PUNISH). **The Emperor reworked:** his blows come quicker (a slam lands at about a second), and after half health he strings two together. New blows: the **swat** (white: a hand swung out and swept across the ice in front of him; parry it on the ring and the hand lies stunned for double damage), the **clap** (red: both hands raised wide and brought together on a circle in front of him; roll out and both lie open) and a **shockwave** from every slam (a thin purple ring running out over the ice: jump it or roll). Less to stand out of: icicles fall only when everyone keeps far from him for a while, he weeps rarely and with fewer tears, and the wingbeat comes less often. He has a **posture bar** too: blows on his hands and faces, parries and blows rolled through fill it, and full, he **slumps** onto the ice with every face and both hands open. Each of his blows has its own sound. **Then, a new way to fight:** Hellcraft's own combat, built for smooth movement: every move blends into the next instead of snapping, in first and third person alike. **Weapons swing (part 2):** with a sword, an axe or a mace the attack key swings the weapon, with a wind-up, and the blow strikes **everything in its path** when it comes round (monsters and players; anything else only if you aim at it; never through walls). **Combos:** click again as a swing ends and the next move follows: a sword cuts, cuts back and thrusts with a lunge; an axe chops and rips upward; a mace smashes and sweeps. **Heavy blows:** hold the key instead of tapping: slower, costs stamina, hits about twice as hard. Each weapon has its own animations, seen by everyone, and moves play faster with Haste. A chain deals about what vanilla clicking did, a little more for keeping it going. Looking at a block with nothing to fight, the key still mines. Spears, tridents, tools and bare hands are as before. **And from part 1:** **Stamina:** a thin gold bar over your hunger; rolling and guarding spend it and it comes back a moment after you stop. **Dodge roll for everyone:** press the Dash key (Left Alt) to roll the way you're moving (standing still, you hop back): a real forward roll over the shoulders, and in the middle of it blows pass through you, a boss's marks too. Sidestep leggings no longer unlock the dash: they make the roll cheaper, longer and safe for longer. **Guard with your weapon:** hold right-click with a sword, an axe, a mace or a hell weapon (and nothing to use in your other hand) and it turns aside most of a blow from the front, at a cost in stamina; out of stamina, the guard breaks. Arrows and blasts still get through, and a shield still blocks everything and comes first. **Parry:** raise the guard just before the blow lands and nothing gets through, the attacker reels, and you get stamina back; a boss's white flash can be parried with a weapon now. **Hits have weight:** your blows hold for a frame and kick the view, and the target shows it (blood, bone chips or sparks). **Hell weapons:** right-click now guards, so the Blood Art is struck from the guard: hold right-click, then press attack (the Blood Oath is still sneak + right-click, and the Blood Pickaxe is unchanged). Turn all of it off with `/hellcraft config combatOverhaul false` (vanilla combat, and Sidestep's old dash). **The hell weapons fight their own way (part 3):** the **Bloodletter** makes four quick cuts, the third a spin that catches everything round you and the last a thrust that opens the deepest wound; held, it lunges a long way. The **Reaper of Minos** makes two great sweeps and a full turn that drags what it reaps towards you. The **Tithe Axe** chops, rips upward and, held, comes down in a slam that shakes the ground round where it lands. Their blades trail blood through the air (embers too, once infernal), and each Blood Art now has a body: the Bloodletter's lunge, the Reaper's turn, the axe raised over the head. **Before that, 3.4.1 (which was only ever a beta, so it is all in 3.5):** **Find, name and travel to any Blood Altar:** the ruined altars scattered through Hell (a respawn anchor on crying obsidian among broken pillars, with a chest of offerings) and the altars players build are places now. Right-click one and it's remembered: it shows in your travel menu and on your Map of Hell (a purple mark), and stand beside it and type /rest name and then a name to name it (only you see it). If someone breaks it, it leaves your travel menu. **Ruined altars are safe camps**, like small Virgil's Rests: no monster appears within 10 blocks of one, a monster that walks in is thrown back out by the soul fire, and the circles' hazards leave you alone there (until someone breaks the altar). **Three more guardians remade:** Cerberus is the Great Worm (three heads on long thick necks over a bloated, mangy body sagging into the mud), Plutus the wolf-headed banker (his belly turning to gold, his cloak sewn with coins, his rolling coin stamped with his wolf) and Phlegyas the drowned ferryman (weed in his beard, the sullen's chains across his chest, a huge black oar), all with new moves on the same timing. **The blood armour redrawn, and the infernal armour looks its own:** blood armour is crimson plate with bone trim (a crested helm with burning eye slits, a ribcage on the chest, a spine down the back, knee guards and a belt), and infernal armour is blackened steel with brass and molten cracks glowing through, worn and in your inventory, so you can tell them apart at a glance. **Fixes:** one right-click no longer uses a Hellcraft item twice (two Vigil Candles from a stack, or two Blood Hearts): Blood Hearts, Fragments, Lucifer's Bane, Vigil Candles and the Blood Altar's heart shortcuts now have a short cooldown, shown on the hotbar; every Hellcraft item, block and creature has a proper name everywhere (some screens showed `item.hellcraft...` keys); travel sets you down beside a ruined altar, not inside its chest, and the Map of Hell's key no longer cuts its hints off on smaller screens. Before that, **3.4.0:** **Penitents on Purgatory:** each terrace now has souls working off their sin: the proud bowed under great stones, the envious huddled against the cliff, the wrathful walking in smoke, the slothful running round, the greedy lying in the dust, the gluttons standing under the fruit they can't reach, and the lustful walking through fire. They're scenery: they can't be hurt, keep off the stairs and only sigh (turn them off with the damnedSouls setting, like Hell's damned). **A lighter Map of Hell:** it keeps a small overview of everywhere you've been and loads the close-up pieces only as you zoom in, so a big explored world no longer eats memory or stutters when you open the map; zoomed in, the painted map of unexplored ground is sharp instead of blurry. **Every gatehouse tower has a door onto the wall:** in a few towers the stair blocked it; those now open on the far side, onto a walk along the wall top. **Lust's wind, twice as thick and different in every world:** a new world has 72 wind streams instead of 36, and where each one starts, how it bends and which way down it lands by are drawn from the world's seed, so no two worlds blow alike (worlds made before keep their first 36). **Name your Rests:** stand in a Virgil's Rest and type /rest name and then a name: it goes by that name in your travel menu, on your Map of Hell and in your Journal (only you see it; /rest name alone gives back its own name). Every Rest also has a clear name of its own now (its circle and its road, or its quarter for the four between the roads), so the travel menu no longer lists eight Rests per circle under the same name. **Small fixes:** Avarice's terrace floor is trodden earth instead of pale sand (it looked like snow), and Gluttony's water is a murky green so the puddles on its road show up. No new world needed, except for Lust's new wind (Purgatory's new floor shows where it hasn't been generated yet).

**From the 3.0 playtest:** the map is half as wide again (radius 5,250), so every circle is wider. **A shield blocks a boss's blow the moment it's raised**, so a late block on a white flash counts. Lust's **lovers** dive one pair at a time, and a dive blocked with a shield knocks them to the ground, stunned. Danger marks show over Cocytus's snow. The **roads** climb on stairs, some askew, with cracked and broken stones, and one circle's stone mixes into the next. **Lucifer is harder:** his fight runs faster and hits harder; the Fallen Seraph's wings turn most blows aside until you block his white slash (then he takes extra), and trading blows draws a riposte; the Emperor picks his blows at random, with little rest, and has new ones (both hands at once, a hand dragged round the ice, a frozen breath that sweeps a red wedge) while icicles keep falling. The climb out after him says plainly what is happening. Phlegyas swings his oar right round at arm's length (the purple ring is its reach), the Minotaur charges on both legs, and the bosses' and monsters' skins, fur and metal, and the blood armour's icons, are redrawn. **Every boss and monster has a new, more lifelike body** (faces with brows, noses and jaws, hands with fingers, wings of real feathers, layered clothes and armour; Cerberus bites forward, the centaurs aim their bows ahead, the harpies' wings beat the right way and the Malebranche keep their hooks in hand), and the Blood Heart and Tithe Axe have new icons. **The Wood of the Suicides is a thicket** now: gnarled trees with branches at head height and black thorns that slow you and tear you unless you sneak (sneaking is also what keeps the trees from screaming); the roads through it stay clear. **Angels fill Paradiso:** a host wheels round every sphere's island and a swarm flies in and out of the Celestial Rose, and the Angelic Guard are real angels now. **Make a new world.**

**New since phase 7 (Phase 8 so far):** ops can give anyone a testing kit with `/hellcraft loadout [players] [kit]` (works in single player with cheats on): the journey kits `upper`, `lower`, `lucifer` and `paradiso` give about what you'd have by then, hearts included (10, 12, 15, 18), to test the bosses fairly without the grind; `/hellcraft arena <boss> [lair] [players]` takes you to the edge of any boss's arena; `full` (the default) and `blood` give everything at once (maxed armour, every weapon, 16 ender pearls, 16 enchanted golden apples, totems). Every guardian of Hell now says something about Lucifer as it falls, and the Journal's Codex has a page on **the Emperor** that fills in, one piece for each guardian you beat. In boss fights your **style rank** now has its own panel on the right of the screen (the rank, a meter to the next one, and what just scored or cost you). Beat Minos, Cerberus, Plutus, Farinata or the Minotaur and its lair keeps a **lift** for you: stand in the soul fire in the middle for 3 seconds to go down to the next circle. The Foundry Halls' pillars have **chain-lifts** instead of ladders: stand on the plate by the chain to ride up to the arm, sneak to float down. In Paradiso, Beatrice gives the tips. **Every guardian of Hell now has four lairs** in its circle, one in each quarter of Hell (Phlegyas a landing by every watchtower, the Furies one inside every gate of Dis): fight it in whichever is nearest. There are **eight Virgil's Rests in every circle** now (four more between the roads, at the foot of a way down; Malebolge keeps four, its other bridges have the fake ones), and the travel menu has pages. **Make a new world** for the new lairs' level floors (in an old world they're built where the ground lies). The **relics** are real items now: the Halo is a gold circlet you wear, the Seraph Wings have white feathers, and Beatrice's Rose shows its hour's wait on the item.

**New in phase 7 (Purgatory and Paradiso):** **Purgatory** is its own world now, a mountain island in a starlit sea before dawn (the burrow and the climb out after Lucifer still take you there). **The Ascent** on its summit takes those who have beaten Lucifer up into **Paradiso**, also its own world: nine spheres of floating islands stacked one above the other, each with its own look, and the **Celestial Rose** in the Empyrean on top. In each sphere cross from the arrival isle to the great island, pass its short **trial** (gather the lights only you can see, against the clock on Mercury, catching them on Venus, in order on Jupiter's Eagle, up Jacob's Ladder on Saturn; beat the Angelic Guard on Mars), then stand in the **column of light** on the departure isle to rise to the next (hold sneak to sink back down). Falling can't hurt you there: angels catch you. The compass points the way. In the ninth sphere **the Seraph**, a six-winged angel on a real body, is the last trial (block its white wing-blow, run IN close for its Gloria, jump the turning heavens); beaten, it gives a **Halo**. Saturn gives **Seraph Wings**, the Rose's bell **Beatrice's Rose**. There are **no strongholds** any more (the End is vanilla and out of reach), and the Journal's second page tells the whole journey. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 6 (the Nether: the Forge of Dis):** the Nether is built from scratch round **the Great Forge**, Vulcan's smithy on a mesa at its centre (0, 0). Round the mesa lies **the Slag Sea**: cross it on the cooling crust, and keep moving, because it cracks under you and melts (four causeways of crust run straight to the stairs up the mesa). Beyond it lie four regions: **the Foundry Halls** (north: rivers of lava and great pillars with ladders), **the Chainlands** (east: islands hung on chains over the lava, joined by bridges), **the Ash Wastes** (south: piglins, bastions and fortresses) and **the Cyclops Quarries** (west: terraces with ramps, and the Cyclopes' camps). A column of heat rises over the Forge, and in the Nether the compass points to it. **Vulcan** fights on a real body now, with an entrance and the danger language (block his white hammer blow, jump his shockwave, step off his chain's red line; at half health the floor's seams burst). **The Cyclopes** are mini-bosses by their fires: block the maul, dodge the boulder, jump the stamp. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 5 (Lucifer):** Cocytus is cold: the cold builds while you're away from fire, so light the **braziers** on the ice (flint and steel or a torch); they stay lit for everyone. Every few minutes **Lucifer's wings beat** all over Hell, and from the Well of Giants you see them turning far off in the fog like a windmill. His pit is now a 70-block floor of ice. Step onto it and the fight starts in 30 seconds (sooner once everyone near is in), with a warning before the point of no return. **The Fallen Seraph** comes down in a cutscene and duels you in the danger language (block the white, dodge the red and purple); at half health he snaps and the traitors rise. Break him and **the mountain in the pit opens its eyes:** the Three-Faced Emperor, 10 times your height, who can only be hurt on the hands and faces he leaves down (block his bite to keep a face down longer) and whose wingbeat you hide from behind the six ice pillars. Beat him and you climb down his side and out to Purgatory. **From the Phase 4 play session:** the pit has no holes left to hide in, the lairs and Rests are spread out so each sits in its own circle, the roads are ruins with slab steps, Antaeus's arm swings the right way (and every boss's blows face forward), Geryon flies you a long way down, Lust has many more wind streams, and the ferry no longer drags you through blocks and lands you inside the Walls of Dis. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 4 (Lower Hell, Dis to the Giants):** each lower circle has a rule to play with. **Heresy:** the tombs blast fire in turn (watch the red circles and cross between blasts). **Phlegethon:** ford the river of blood at its shallows while the centaurs on the banks look away. **The Wood of the Suicides:** sneak, or the trees scream and call the harpies. **The Burning Sands:** fire falls in waves; shelter under the rock arches. **Malebolge:** nothing is what it seems: chests that breathe are mimics, a Rest that isn't on your compass is a trap, thieves snatch from your pack, and the Malebranche hook you along red lines (and their captain Malacoda will kindly show you a bridge). Five new guardians on real bodies: **the Furies** (who call **Medusa**: don't look at her while her eyes glow), **Farinata** in his burning tomb, **the Minotaur** and **Geryon**. Beat Geryon and he flies you down the great cliff; **Antaeus** sets you down on the ice of Cocytus from the Well. New monsters: heretics, centaurs, harpies, mimics, thieves and the Malebranche. **Make a new world** (the guardians' lairs and Antaeus moved). **From the Phase 4 play session:** the bosses fight at 60% of their old pace (longer wind-ups, warnings and parry windows; `bossTempo`), Geryon sinks low after each attack and the Furies land after their talons, so they can be hit, Lucifer hits for 70%, and more hearts help again (boss hits grow half as fast with them). The hell weapons and blood armour are real items now (and become infernal items at a Hellforge; old ones keep working). New: five enchantments found only in one circle each, among them **Sidestep** (leggings), which adds a **Dash** key (Left Alt) that dodges boss blows.

**Phase 3 (Upper Hell, Limbo to Wrath):** each upper circle has a rule to play with instead of a debuff. **Lust:** white wind streams carry you down the circle (step in; sneak to let go). **Gluttony:** the mud swallows whoever stands still (keep moving, or stand on roots, stone or planks). **Greed:** gold draws hoarders that steal it (stash it in an ender chest). **Wrath:** hands drag swimmers under where the Styx bubbles (keep to the roads, or take a boat). Limbo's **Noble Castle** stands on the east road, with shades who talk, trade and give Codex pages. New set-pieces in every circle (soul flocks over Lust, rotting trees and sunken feast tables in the Mire, coin hills, vaults and giant scales in Greed, fog, reeds, boardwalks and watchtowers in the Fen). **Cerberus, Plutus and Phlegyas** have real bodies and fights in the danger language; light the east watchtower's beacons to call Phlegyas, and any watchtower's to call his ferry to Dis. New monsters: the lovers, the gluttons, the hoarders and the wrathful. Fair play: no PvP in the Dark Wood, the Shore and Limbo, two hours of newcomer protection, and Cain's Mark for killing much weaker souls. **From the first play session:** what characters say now appears in a **dialogue box** above the hotbar instead of the chat; the Fen is lighter and its fog thinner; walking into Phlegyas's ring of braziers wakes him too; the older bosses no longer show the mob inside their model when hit by a potion effect; and the Spines over Cocytus are bent and broken instead of straight and mirrored. **Make a new world** for the new set-pieces and the new Spines.

**Phase 2 (boss tech, proven on Minos):** Minos has a real, animated body. Waking him plays a short cutscene (skippable once seen) with his name card. His fight speaks the danger language: **red** on the ground means get out, a **white** flash means raise your shield now (a block in time staggers him), **purple** can't be blocked, so jump it. Meeting him opens his entry in the Journal's Codex (J). The written guide book is gone: its pages are in the Journal.

**Phase 1, the new map:** Hell is 7,000 blocks across (border at 3,500). Four paved roads (east, south, west and north) lead from the Gate of Hell to the Well of Giants, and every cliff has a way down every 30 degrees. Entering a circle shows a card saying what it does and what to bring. A compass at the top of the screen points to the next way down and the nearest Virgil's Rest. **M** opens the Map of Hell and **J** the Pilgrim's Journal. **Make a new world:** worlds from older builds have the old map.

**Every player installs Hellcraft**, the same version as the server:
- **Modrinth App / Prism Launcher:** download `Hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3.mrpack` and import it (it installs Minecraft 26.3, Fabric and Fabric API for you). Use it for single player and to join a Hellcraft server.
- **Official Minecraft Launcher:** download `hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3-mods.zip` and follow `INSTALL.txt`.
- **Single player:** Create New World, World tab, World Type: **Inferno** (turn on *Allow Commands* for `/hellcraft goto <zone>`).

**Servers:** use `hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3.jar` with the Docker setup in the README (`itzg/minecraft-server:java25`, `VERSION` 26.3). Only port 25565 is needed. Players without the matching Hellcraft are told what to install.
